title: On Psalm 29
english: It has not become a desert the inhabited world (Ps 28:8). The previously mentioned voice of the Lord prepares the allegorically called deer. And these are souls, to kill the acts of the body by the spirit and to strip the impious one by the spirit through the lips by imitation of God.

And the voice of the Lord will work for her and a revelation of woods (Ps 28:9), so that the beasts lurking in them might be made manifest, they are lifted up as deer. And a wood is a natural place of fruitless trees; and the wood is revealed when the fruitless trees in it are being cut down by the axe of the Word and are being thrown into fire.

When that which overshadows the progress of men is removed, then everyone, having ceased from the manifold error, will speak glory in the temple of God (Ps 28:10). The sitting of God signifies his strength to remain unshakeable and incorruptible forever (Ps 28:10). For indeed he distributes it to those perishing through turning: 'You sitting for the age, and we perishing for the age.' And here the permanence of his kingdom is presented. For this reason, 'And the Lord King is established for the age' (Ps 28:10), having no end to his kingdom.

But he who speaks according to the history says that David the king, having been eager to build something tangible for the Lord, was forbidden by God speaking to him (Ps 29:1): 'Not you shall build for me something, because you are a man of war from your youth, but he who comes out of your loins shall build for me something.' Having been persuaded by the oracle, David ceased from building, but he pre-arranged the materials for the building. As he says, he prepared the materials, and also having composed the psalm, he left it as one of the necessary things, and how, after the temple having been built and dedicated, it might be struck with singing and chanting by those appointed to this.

He says that he will be saved (Ps 29:4) if God does not let him descend to him, or after descending, having brought him up. These things are said economically and as from the face of Christ, who having descended his soul on our behalf and having given it and having risen from the dead by the good pleasure of God and Father, toward whom he says humanly: '...
"For You did not abandon my soul to the pit, a pit called by name; I say with confidence: You saved me from those descending into the pit" (Ps 29:6c).

The end of the day prepares the true light; they weep in the evening—that is, having come into being at the beginning of the night—while the beginning of the day rejoices, having occurred for them with the rising of the sun of righteousness (Ps 29:6d). This applies to both: the weeping of the circumcised when the sun of righteousness rises for them, and the joy of the Gentiles when the saving word shines upon them.

One must hear prosperity through spiritual fruitfulness, so that the seed of Jesus becomes a hundredfold and the other generations of virtue are multiplied (Ps 29:7). In this prosperity, having been evidenced through these things, I will say that I remain firm and immovable, never to be shaken for ever. And one must cry out thus: "In my prosperity, I shall not be shaken for ever" (Ps 29:7); for through his works he cries out, "If I were in the aforementioned prosperity, I would be unshakeable, not being turned aside by the adversary."

Bodily beauty appears through the symmetry and proportion of the limbs (Ps 29:8a), but the beauty of the soul is in the harmony and symphony of all perfected virtues, having symmetry and proportion in all activities according to reason, and the harmony of the soul's powers in proportion. "Grant this beauty to me, O Lord, according to your will." For having done your will and that of the Father in heaven, he took it up, since everyone having become conformed to the image of the Son of God has received beauty from God, having been united with the Lord's will.

He who, through doing material things and thinking of earthly things, being as dust and persisting in sin, will not confess to God, nor announce the truth to Him, being led astray through morals and knowledge (Ps 29:10c-d).

It is to be noted that "became" does not mean "always being," but also signifies a relationship toward someone. If such a voice were ever to occur regarding the Savior, it signifies a relationship toward Him and not merely being (Ps 29:11b-13). "You turned my weeping into joy for me." The voice of weeping signifies the emotion, just as the very act of the hands placing them on the chest demonstrates it.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Multiplicity of the Human Spirit
english: One who has not become aware in the consciousness of his own sins, and who has not actively awakened his sensation through spiritual hands, changing from being consumed by grief, will receive the fruit of the Spirit as joy. The phrase 'You have turned' signifies a change from cutting and grieving into joy; and 'I shall not be confounded' (Ps 30:2) is said instead of 'I shall not know'. He who sings glory while saying these things to God possesses a right conduct and sincere knowledge.

He who has hoped to reach the end of what is laid up for the saints, and who will not be put to shame for ever, has placed such an expectation upon the Lord. 'In your righteousness, he says, save me' (Ps 30:3) (not by any other than your only-begotten [Son]) 'from those surrounding me and bring me out from those intending to fight against me' (Ps 30:3). And since our cry may not reach your height, 'Incline your ear to me' (Ps 30:4) so that you may descend to accompany me; for the existence of this means that, having received my prayer, you will immediately deliver me by your wills.

And here 'Make me a hiding place' (Ps 30:4) signifies a protector for the one being protected. It is also worthy that those near a refuge should have God become a salvation for them, just as one is saved unharmed while remaining enclosed by an impregnable and unassailable fortress. This I have often and always attempted, as [the Psalmist says], 'You are my strength and my refuge, since your name is my stronghold; for I am your man and your servant' (Ps 30:3). Even if I am not worthy to receive what I ask, because of your goodness you will guide me toward salvation and sustain me, providing me with your heavenly bread (Ps 30:5).

Diligence belongs to the good; the body is not so much to be wounded by enemies, for the war does not seek to deceive him with phantoms and terrors, but rather it seeks not to strike the flesh but to wound the mind from before; the spirit places itself into the hands of God, being able to guard it. And the Savior, having been hung upon the stake, his hands and feet having been pierced according to the prophecy, 'Into your hands I shall commit myself' (Ps 30:6), has used the hands of God, which are none other than his providential and protective powers, to be exercised.

It should be noted that the spirit of man is spoken of in many ways. For in the [prophecy of the] Virgin, where it is said she is to be holy in spirit and body, spirit refers to the intellect. But according to James (as the body without spirit is dead), the designation of 'spirit' signifies nothing other than the soul. And in the [passage] 'For what are the things of man, except the spirit of man which is in him?', it is shown to be nothing other than the spirit joined to the soul or being part of it, which is also called conscience; for the conscience of man is the inward thoughts, which are something other than the soul; for the soul is the man, not the inward thoughts.

Regarding the [Psalm] 'the spirit of man having been set in your hands', stand firm to grasp in what way it is meant: 'Into your hands I commit my spirit' (Ps 31:5). And it pleases me that the present text is true according to the three ways. 'Having been seized by enemies, as having become a captive, I will redeem, O Lord, you who are the God of truth and of the truth shared by each of those participating in the truth of the Only-Begotten' (Ps 30:7a). In general, everyone guarding vanity for no reason does this, making the uncertain to be, or making vanity to happen emptily and superfluously. And he who hates this makes those guarding it hateful to God.

The humiliation, on one hand, shows blindness, when it calls for humility, and on the other hand, the harm by enemies. And it is good to see God in both kinds of humiliation. What follows, he considers to be the harm following the humiliation: 'For you have compressed my soul by necessity' (Ps 31:5), saying 'necessities' regarding the circumstances from which the soul, having been rescued, is not enclosed into the hands of the harming enemy. If the 'spaciousness' were to say the same regarding the wide and spacious way (which is the love of pleasure), it would thank it for its stability and for desiring a standing in this life. For it says something like this: being in the place of the earth, where living is slippery and unsafe because of the sliding pleasures, you have given a standing to my soul, so that I might not be carried away there by the passions. But if it were to praise the spaciousness, it would say: 'Since being afflicted, I am not constricted, being more strengthened by pains', or perhaps, 'being widened by the...'

title: Divine Providence and the Hidden Face
english: Glory comes from circumstances, I will say: 'You have set my feet in a wide place' (Ps 30:11c). Not every poor person is weak (for many poor people are strong), nor is one lacking in strength poor; but in spiritual matters, since strength is the same as wealth, the one who is wealthy has strength in good works. He does not wish to say 'I am such a thing'; since, having turned away from the visible wealth (which is not the divine), he says, 'My strength has grown weak.' It is to be noted what it means to say 'is' instead of 'has'; for it is not strength that is weak, but the one who has it, just as we do not say one is ignorant of knowledge, but that one is ignorant. This is in agreement with what was said by Paul concerning Christ: 'That we might become the righteousness of God in him' (2 Cor 5:21). For in these things, he called those having righteousness 'righteousness.'

Those enemies who are lovers of pleasure rather than lovers of God, not only do not feel shame nor seem to suffer reproach for the evil they do, but on the contrary, they take pride, as it has been said concerning them: 'The glory is in their shame.' And they boast over those who become objects of reproach. Therefore, turn away from your boasting and reproach against the Lord; otherwise, they shall rise to reproach and eternal shame. But he who perceives himself to have become in the aforementioned poverty confesses that he is to be reproached. Therefore he says: 'I have become a reproach to all my enemies, but also to all those who draw near to me according to the proverb—that is, to those who hold the same opinion.'

Those who attack me with persistence, perceiving that they have fallen from wealth into poverty, fearing that they might suffer the same, hasten to be outside of my stability. But also, a vessel which formerly was precious and very useful to the master, seemed to have been lost. Because the ear hears the slander of many dwelling around. If a teacher is called a liar by those who seem to be his [disciples] because of the necessity of learning, yet they dwell around and do not remain in the lessons, they do not abide in them. And it is possible to not be so; since the ear hears the slander of many around me, because they do not abide but merely dwell around our things, for this reason I have become a lost vessel. With this, ...

Is it that someone is weak and I am not weak? Is it that someone stumbles and I am not being burned? (Ps 30:16) My lots fall into those things which are covering and guarding by your hands, being profited by them; that is, all things allotted to me according to your judgment, either to flow from them or to suffer; for it does not happen to them by chance. (Ps 30:16a)

Others clarify the word not thus: the powers given, they say, are called their lots, as if they have superiority over teachers or others. They are not in the hands of God. For just as He establishes, so also He distributes kings. Therefore, because some are coming to move this superiority which is present to me, wanting to do so, they will not be able, since all things concerning me are in your hands. (Ps 30:16)

He does not merely hide his goodness from those fearing him (for they see much of it), but the abundance, so that they may not be harmed. (Ps 30:20-21) And it is also good to say: To those fearing you, it is stored up for them. Reveal it to them, so that those having become in perfect love might cast out fear. 'You have made it known to those fearing you' means you have revealed it by energy, so that those having more hope than fear possess it.

Regarding 'Against the sons of men': You say 'men' regarding those having preserved the rational and incorruptible image, but 'their sons' regarding those having become their rational disciples and imitators. And 'hidden from the face of God' you say, meaning that which is not attainable now to knowledge, but will be revealed then, when we shall see Him as He is. With this 'hidden' thing, that which is said by Paul is contrasted: 'made known to men,' that is, His creative and providential nature. For after the 'God revealed' it is said: 'For his invisible attributes, from the creation of the world, are understood and perceived through the works.' (Rom 1:20)

Perhaps also the Savior has the face of God hidden, all that is according to the divinity, but that which is according to the economy is manifest. And since now the Word having become flesh dwells among us, we are being hidden in the mystery of His face, so that we may see Him as we shall see His glory, a glory as of the only-begotten from the Father, full of grace and truth. (John 1:14) But stand firm, if...
